facts.text: Macomb Township is a civil township at the geographic center of Macomb County, north of the county seat of Mount Clemens.
Macomb, also called Macomb Corners, is a community in the northwest part of the township on Romeo Plank Road at 25 Mile Road, near the Middle Branch of the Clinton River.
Waldenburg, in the central part of the township, sits on Romeo Plank Road and the Clinton River, chiefly around 22 Mile Road.
Romeo Plank Road is a historic route that follows the Middle Branch of the Clinton River on its western side.
In 2024, Macomb Township's planning director described the township as very much subdivision-heavy and suburban.
Township Hall was built in the area of the planned Macomb Township Center, a town center concept first planned in 1998 at the end of Broughton Road.
Macomb Corners Park, a 94 acre site on the north side of 25 Mile Road just east of Luchtman Road, has lighted ball diamonds, soccer fields and a walking trail and hosts summer community events.
Waldenburg Park, on 21 Mile Road east of Romeo Plank Road, has an accessible playground, picnic pavilions and a walking trail.

Macomb Township Parks and Recreation hosts an annual Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony at the Macomb Township Recreation Center, with caroling, the arrival of Santa and the lighting of the tree. The 2026 ceremony is Friday, December 4.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Macomb Township, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Macomb Township homes lit for Christmas: crisp rooflines, wrapped yard trees and lit shrubs, with design, installation and takedown after the holidays.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Macomb Township, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Clean rooflines, wrapped trees and lit landscaping for your home. The design, the install, service through the season and the takedown, all handled for you.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Macomb Township is very much a subdivision community, and that changes the brief for a Christmas display. Your house is seen right next to its neighbors, so clean, even lines matter more than sheer volume. A crisp roofline, one well wrapped yard tree and lit shrubs along the walk often say more than a crowded lawn. When homes on a street share similar rooflines, design is what sets one apart. We look at the peaks, the garage, the porch and the landscaping, then plan a display that fits the house and any association guidelines you need to follow. Installation, in-season service and a return trip for takedown after the holidays are all part of the job.
considerations: Standing out on a similar street

When several houses share the same builder's rooflines, small choices make the difference: which peaks to outline, which tree to wrap, warm white or multicolor. We help you pick a look that suits the house without fighting the rest of the street.

Some subdivisions have rules on exterior decorations, lighting hours or placement. Check yours before the season starts. Your estimate describes the planned display in plain terms, which makes it easy to share if your association asks to see it.

Front-facing garages and stacked gables are common on suburban homes, and they are where lines tend to go crooked. Our crews work from the bucket truck where the driveway allows, keeping every run straight across the garage and up each peak.
faq: Can you light my Macomb Township home for Christmas?

Yes. Macomb Township is among the Macomb County communities in our service area, along with Shelby Township. Ask for a free estimate online or by calling (248) 756-8915, and we will arrange a time to see the house and hear what you want.
Can neighbors on the same street book together?

Yes. Neighbors who want matching or complementary displays can request estimates at the same time, and we can plan the designs side by side so the street looks coordinated. Each home still receives its own written estimate describing its own scope of work.
What will the estimate spell out?

We look at the roofline, trees, shrubs and power, hear which look you are after and review any association rules you mention. A written estimate follows, listing the design, the install, in-season service and the post-holiday takedown.

commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Macomb Township, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Subdivision entrances, condo communities, offices and retail properties, lit with care by bucket-truck crews and managed under a single seasonal plan.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: In a township this subdivision-heavy, some of the most important commercial lighting happens at the entrance to a neighborhood. A well lit entry tells residents they are home and gives visitors a good first impression all season. We light entry monuments, wrap the surrounding trees and add light to the landscaping and medians where it fits, with a design the whole association can get behind. Condo communities and managed properties get the same treatment across every building and drive. Offices, medical buildings and retail properties across Macomb Township get a clear design, a written estimate and one team from installation through takedown.
considerations: When a subdivision has more than one entrance, residents notice if they do not match. We design each entrance as part of one look, with consistent colors and spacing, so every way into the neighborhood feels equally cared for through the season.

Association spending is often approved in advance, and decisions may go to a vote. We provide a written estimate with the full scope laid out and can meet a board member or manager on site, so the proposal answers questions before the meeting.

Offices, medical buildings and retail centers want a polished look that suits the property. Building outlines and tall lot trees are handled from the bucket truck, entrances are lit at ground level, and takedown after the season is built into the plan from the start.
faq: Do you light HOA entrances in Macomb Township?

Yes. Subdivision and HOA entrances in Macomb Township are within our service area, and entrance lighting is a core part of our commercial work. Contact us online or at (248) 756-8915 to arrange a look at the entrance with someone from your board.
Can one company handle several properties?

Yes. Property managers with more than one community or building can bring them to us together. We plan each site on its own terms, keep the look consistent where you want it and handle every stage, from design to takedown, across the portfolio.
When should an association approve its holiday lighting?

Early, if possible. Installs for associations and businesses usually run from October into early December, and boards that approve in late summer or early fall have the most installation dates to choose from. Our written estimate gives the board the details it needs to vote.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Macomb Township, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Macomb Township permanent Christmas lights: app-controlled roofline lights for holidays, game days and nightly accents, planned with HOA rules in mind.
permanent-lighting.h1: Permanent Lighting in Macomb Township, MI
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Year-round lighting on your roofline, run from your phone. Warm white in December, orange for Halloween and a soft glow any night, without an install every fall.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Subdivision homes are a natural fit for permanent lighting, and Macomb Township is full of them. Suburban rooflines with a front garage and a peak or two often take a clean, continuous outline well. The lights stay in place along the eaves all year and answer to an app, so the same install covers Christmas, Halloween, Independence Day, game days and ordinary evenings. Schedules bring them on at dusk without anyone flipping a switch. On a street of similar houses, a well planned outline also sets yours apart without shouting. We design the layout, install it and walk you through the app.
considerations: Permanent fixtures are more likely than seasonal lights to need HOA sign-off. Ask your association about exterior lighting and fixture rules early. The written estimate shows where each run will go, so the board has a concrete plan to decide on before any work begins.

Most of the visual impact comes from the front: the garage roofline, the entry peak and any gables facing the street. We plan runs and corners so the outline is continuous and the start and end points look tidy from the sidewalk.

Warm white for December is only the start. Save scenes for Halloween, Valentine's Day and Independence Day, set team colors for game days and schedule a soft nightly accent. You make every change from the app, and nobody climbs a ladder.
faq: Can a Macomb Township home get permanent lighting?

Yes. Permanent roofline lighting is available for homes in Macomb Township, which is part of our Southeast Michigan service area. Your free estimate starts with the roofline and the nearest power, moves on to the occasions you have in mind, and ends with a written plan.
Will permanent lights look out of place in a subdivision?

They should not. By day the lights are meant to blend in with the trim, and the house keeps its everyday look. At night you decide how bold to be, from a subtle warm outline to full holiday color, which keeps things friendly with the neighbors.

In the app you set when the lights come on and go off and which colors or scenes play. A common setup is a warm outline at dusk every evening, holiday colors on the dates you choose and team colors whenever there is a big game.
